  "reasoning": "All captured answers agree with the mathematics except the completeness claim in q-47077. Both options 0 and 1 permit IVT: on [-2,1], the restricted function is exactly x+1 and is continuous, including at its right endpoint. MA's answer [-2,0] is valid, but its rejection of [-2,1] is incorrect. For q-12706, two integrations by parts give the stated antiderivative. For q-8479, x=5\\pi/24+n\\pi/2, so the first two roots multiply to 85\\pi^2/576. For q-82373, the roots in degrees are 45,135,225,315, giving 6075. For q-77809, cosecant cannot have absolute value below 1, excluding I and III. For q-82529, (x,y) maps to (x,-y-x/2), giving vertices (0,0),(1,-1/2),(1,-3/2),(0,-1). For q-82525, (x,y) maps to (y,-x-y/2), producing the same polygon with a different transformation of its interior lettering; option 4 matches. For q-12257, multiplying the clockwise rotation matrix on the left by diag(1/6,1) gives the stated matrix. For q-48430, IVT requires continuity and a target between the endpoint values inclusively. For q-48334, those endpoint values are 2 and 6. For q-105684, f(1)=2 and f(4)=66; k=1 is outside the guaranteed range and below every function value on the interval. For q-47101, g(2)=0 and g(4)=-12; g is nonpositive throughout [2,4], so k=1 is excluded. For q-78542 and q-105701, respectively two and three disjoint open subintervals force distinct crossings; piecewise linear interpolation attains these minimum counts. For q-118090 and q-118135, the standard exponential limits give e^{xy} and e^{xy^2} for fixed real x,y. No submitted grades or earlier answers are supplied; MA evidence comes from each question's own captured worked solution.",
